svg.title: Four order studies, four different jobs
svg.desc: Matched CVs, May 2025 (Rozado): 22 models chose between two CVs for a job. The first-listed candidate got 63.5% of picks, and 21 of the 22 leaned that way. No right answer. Claude 3.5 Sonnet was the Claude in the test. Colours and CVs, June 2025 onward (Yin and colleagues): Options built to be close. Strong order effects that changed with quality: the first option among good ones, a later one among poor ones. No right answer. The newest Claude was Sonnet 4. Agents booking hotels, August 2026 (Wadi and Ma): 7,000 sessions picking from 100 listings. Position mattered less as reasoning effort rose, and Claude Sonnet 5 at high effort showed no detectable effect. GPT 6 Luna showed one at every level. Exam questions, October 2026 (Li and colleagues): The right answer was forced into one slot of a multiple-choice test. The largest gap was about 4 points for GPT-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4, against about 21 for the smallest model. Thinking models were "nearly immune". There is an answer key here, and no Claude. None of these asked a current Claude to make a close workplace call, which is the gap my trial tries to fill.

the effect. Each row tests a different kind of choice.
